items.title: Theni jailbreak: Inmate’s mother alleges police violence on rearrest, moves Madras HC
items.summary: The mother of two male inmates who escaped from Theni jail has moved the Madras High Court seeking immediate medical treatment for her sons and two other remand prisoners who were allegedly assaulted by prison officials when they were rearrested. She has also sought an independent judicial inquiry into the matter. In a writ petition filed on November 2, K Arumugathammal, the mother of Meenakshi Sundaram (26) and Thirupathi (22), alleged that the four prisoners sustained multiple injuries after being assaulted by prison warders while in custody. She has sought a direction to the Tamil Nadu government and prison authorities to refer the injured prisoners to the Government Mohan Kumaramangalam Medical College Hospital in Salem for complete medical examination and necessary treatment including specialist care. The petition also names Solai Mugileswaran (19) and Sabarinathan (24) as the other injured prisoners currently lodged at the Salem Central Prison. items.title: We don't want to be the largest firm, we want to be the finest: Amar Gupta and Vivek Chandy on JSA turning 35
items.summary: To mark 35 years of its existence, JSA Advocates and Solicitors underwent a rebranding exercise , adding an infinity symbol to its logo. The symbol, among other things, signifies the "continuity of an institution built to outlast any individual". And this is a philosophy put into practice by its managing partners. [Watch Video] Most law firm leaders at the peak of their careers plan to keep their clients for as long as they can. Vivek Chandy and Amar Gupta plan to give theirs away. "I could very well continue working to 75, decide that I want to move to another firm and take my book of business with me. But that's not the JSA model," says Chandy, now in his third term as joint managing partner. Both expect to retire in five or six years, following founders Jyoti Sagar and Berjis Desai , who left their entire books with younger partners. Gupta and Chandy spoke to Bar & Bench’s Pallavi Saluja about equity-weighted elections, a lateral hiring spree, a new GIFT City office, foreign firms and AI. Edited excerpts follow. items.title: How BJP helped ‘Judicial Krishnamoorthy’ get five elephants to Tamil Nadu
items.summary: Judicial Krishnamoorthy next to the elephant He stands next to Durga in a snap clicked just after the tiny 5-year-old elephant was pulled out of a truck that had carried her all the way from Assam to Madurai’s Meenakshi Ammal temple. A middle-aged man with a stoop and a moustache, beaming in his white shirt and a cream-coloured veshti. His name is Vaidyanathan Krishnamoorthy. Seva Trust, a non-descript religious charity run by his wife, Anuradha Subramanian, gifted Durga to the temple in September 2026. Durga, so young she had probably just been weaned, wasn’t the only one to make this long journey from Assam to Tamil Nadu. Anuradha’s Seva Trust also donated four more elephants – three pre-adolescent and one barely adolescent – to temples in Nagapattinam, Kanchipuram and Tiruvannamalai. Elephant Durga Nagapattinam’s Vaitheeswaran Koil got Rupsing , said to be 13 years old. The Arulmigu Anmachaleswarar Temple in Tiruvannamalai bagged Hiralal and Shiva , said to be 8 and 6 years old, respectively. And Kanchi Kamakoti in Kanchipuram got Bijuli , said to be 5 years old.
